name: Telegram
description: Telegram is a cloud messaging platform with personal chats, groups, channels, bots, Mini Apps, an HTTP Bot API, OIDC Login, and the MTProto client protocol.
agentUseSummary: Telegram is not currently installable as a persistent Relay provider. Telegram OIDC offers Authorization Code with PKCE for identity and optional linked-bot direct messaging, but documents only a one-hour access token and ID token with no refresh token or programmatic revocation endpoint. Bot tokens grant full bot control, while MTProto uses phone/code/2FA client sessions; neither is delegated account OAuth.

blocked.label: Create a persistent OIDC connection
blocked.description: Telegram documents one-hour OIDC access and ID tokens but no refresh token or Relay-callable programmatic revocation lifecycle.

blocked.label: Retain linked-bot messaging access
blocked.description: The telegram:bot_access scope grants persistent direct-message authority without a documented per-Relay-connection upstream revoke operation.

blocked.label: Custody a bot token
blocked.description: A BotFather token gives anyone who holds it full control over the bot and belongs to the bot owner, not the connecting Telegram user.

blocked.label: Create a Telegram client session
blocked.description: MTProto phone, code, passkey, QR, and 2FA authorization creates a persistent client encryption-key session and must not be represented as OAuth.

blocked.label: Access Telegram data or messaging
blocked.description: Profiles, phone numbers, personal chats, groups, channels, messages, bot management, direct messaging, files, contacts, and every read/write remain unavailable.

approvalProfiles.label: Unavailable
approvalProfiles.description: No agent actions can be enabled until Telegram documents a persistent refresh/revocation lifecycle or Relay approves a separate ephemeral-login or bot product.

runtimeSupport.description: Telegram's current identity, bot, and MTProto lifecycles do not support a durable revocable Relay provider connection.

providerSetup.blocker: Telegram OIDC does not document refresh tokens or programmatic revocation, telegram:bot_access has no per-installation revoke operation, Bot API tokens grant full bot control, and MTProto is a persistent client login rather than OAuth.
providerSetup.nextAction: Do not request Telegram credentials or show Connect. Reconsider after official refresh/revocation documentation, or after a separate product decision accepts an ephemeral identity-only login or a Relay-owned bot with explicit bot-access disconnect risk.

evidence.supports: Telegram documents OIDC Authorization Code with S256 PKCE, openid/profile/phone/telegram:bot_access scopes, and one-hour access/ID tokens, but no refresh token, UserInfo endpoint, or programmatic revocation endpoint.
Telegram states that BotFather issues bot tokens and anyone holding one has full control over the bot.
Telegram documents bot-token revocation through BotFather, which rotates the bot credential rather than revoking one user's Relay installation.
Telegram MTProto user authorization binds a persistent encryption key to a user through phone/code, QR, passkey, or 2FA client login rather than delegated OAuth.
